effective_prompt: Use the $otel-audit skill. Before doing or saying anything else, run exactly this one read-only command and wait for it to complete: cat .agents/skills/otel-audit/SKILL.md. Do not combine that read with pwd or any other command, and do not emit commentary before or during the read. Then follow the skill. $otel-audit

rules.rule: Identifies app.py and pyproject.toml as the relevant entrypoint and dependency files.
Enumerates the Flask task CRUD routes and health route.
Reports no opentelemetry packages and no SDK initialization.
Mentions opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask as the auto-instrumentation gap.
Calls out request duration, rate, errors, and OTLP exporter configuration.

Classifies the missing supported stdlib application-log bridge and local Splunk Observability Studio exporter as a required default gap, while preserving explicit opt-out/operator ownership and keeping cloud forwarding limited to traces and metrics. Resolves the current local OTLP endpoint from configuration or advertised receiver state before using the 4317/4318 fallbacks, preserves a configured non-default port, and does not require application startup to query Obstudio.

checks.reason: The audit correctly identifies app.py as the Flask entrypoint and pyproject.toml as the dependency manifest.
checks.evidence: service/app.py: "app = Flask(__name__)"; service/pyproject.toml: "dependencies = [\n    \"flask>=3.1\",\n]". service/.observe/otel-audit.json, Entry point: "Flask CLI auto-discovers app.py:app"; Manifest cites "pyproject.toml:1-11".

checks.reason: The audit enumerates all six declared routes, covering task CRUD and health.
checks.evidence: service/app.py declares @app.get("/health"), @app.get("/tasks"), @app.get("/tasks/<int:task_id>"), @app.post("/tasks"), @app.patch("/tasks/<int:task_id>"), and @app.delete("/tasks/<int:task_id>"). service/.observe/otel-audit.json, Route source: "GET /health; GET /tasks; GET /tasks/<int:task_id>; POST /tasks; PATCH /tasks/<int:task_id>; DELETE /tasks/<int:task_id>".

checks.reason: The audit accurately reports no declared OpenTelemetry packages or SDK initialization in the inspected service.
checks.evidence: service/pyproject.toml lists only "flask>=3.1"; service/app.py imports "atexit", "signal", and "Flask, jsonify, request" without OTel setup. service/.observe/otel-audit.json states "No OTel declared" and "no provider: no TracerProvider, registration, exporter, lazy helper or external bootstrap configured". trace.jsonl, item_13, reports "provider_construction": [] and "provider_registration": [].

checks.reason: The audit explicitly identifies the missing Flask auto-instrumentation package and proposes its integration.
checks.evidence: service/pyproject.toml declares only "flask>=3.1". service/.observe/otel-audit.json, OTEL-002: "opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask is absent"; required_fix: "Add opentelemetry-instrumentation-flask and call FlaskInstrumentor().instrument_app(app) once".

checks.reason: The findings cover request duration, request rate, errors, and OTLP exporter configuration.
checks.evidence: service/app.py includes error responses such as "return {\"error\": \"not found\"}, 404" without telemetry. service/.observe/otel-audit.json names "http.server.request.duration" and explains "histogram count provides request rate and status-based error rate". OTEL-001 requires "OTLP/HTTP batching/readers" and lists "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT", "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL", and trace/metric endpoint overrides.

checks.reason: The audit treats the supported stdlib logging bridge and local Studio export as a required default gap. It preserves explicit opt-out and other operator exporter ownership, restricts cloud configuration to traces and metrics, and requires endpoint discovery before fallback. Available repository configuration was inspected without finding a receiver; the fallback is explicitly conditional rather than presented as discovered. The plan preserves non-default ports and excludes Studio queries from application startup.
checks.evidence: service/app.py emits app.logger.warning("runtime request completed") and app.logger.warning("runtime shutdown completed") without a bridge. service/.observe/otel-audit.json, OTEL-003, has "priority": "required" and "instrument_mode": "default"; its fix requires "opentelemetry-instrumentation-logging LoggingInstrumentor bridge", "current bridge-owned handler rather than the deprecated SDK LoggingHandler", and a normal profile setting "OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp". It says "honor none and other operator exporter branches without supplementing them"; logs.disabled adds "An explicit other exporter stays operator-owned". Cloud boundary: "Do not add cloud log endpoints, tokens, headers, exporters or forwarding flags" and move generic headers to "trace/metric variables". Local receiver evidence states "No Studio status tool was available; no receiver endpoint/protocol in checked-in files" and permits fallback "only after higher-precedence configuration discovery is exhausted". trace.jsonl, item_5, records reading "service/app.py service/pyproject.toml service/Makefile"; item_13 reports "runtime_configuration": []. The runtime.receiver.nondefault scenario requires "http://127.0.0.1:14318/v1/traces, /v1/metrics and /v1/logs", "no hardcoded 4318 override", and "Application startup makes no Studio status/discovery or route-registration calls".
